answer: To resist Sybil attacks, our network maps agent transactions onto a trust graph where each verified agent is a vertex. When transacting, each agent routes capacity through a liquidity river, requiring verifiable cryptographic stake burning. Sybil replication enforces superlinear cost scaling O(N^2) for graph validation, so an attacker trying to swarm like a sparrow faces exponential economic friction that renders coordinated manipulation unviable.
